title: The Nexus Between Clean Energy Transition and Economic Growth: Evidence from Saudi Arabia
content: This study examines the relationship between clean energy transition and economic growth in Saudi Arabia during 1990–2024, emphasizing the moderating role of financial development. The autoregressive distributed lag model is employed to estimate short- and long-run relationships, while quantile ARDL and wavelet coherence analyses assess robustness, distributional heterogeneity, and time–frequency dynamics. The findings confirm a stable long-run relationship among economic growth, clean energy transition, financial development, government expenditure, and energy use. Clean energy transition positively affects economic growth in both the short and long run, and this effect remains robust across growth quantiles. However, financial development exerts a negative direct effect and weakens the clean energy transition's contribution to growth. Marginal effects show that the clean energy transition promotes growth at low levels of financial development, becomes insignificant at the average level, and turns negative at high levels. Government expenditure offers only a weak short-run stimulus, while energy use adversely affects growth. The results highlight the need to align financial-sector reform, green finance, public investment, and energy-efficiency policies to maximize the economic benefits of Saudi Arabia’s clean energy transition.
